title: n8n Workflows: How They Work and Examples (2026 Guide)
summary: n8n workflows start with a trigger and flow through connected nodes passing data along. You'll know the structure and what makes each execution work.
body_markdown:
## Running the same lead workflow in Activepieces


Rebuild the lead workflow by hand in Activepieces and it comes to three steps: a Catch Webhook trigger, a Google Sheets row, and a Slack message, with both apps among the 768 integrations in the open source monorepo.


If plan and hosting are still the open question, treat it as a pilot: nothing is imported or converted from n8n, so it's not a migration.


### Building workflows with integrations and webhooks


Inside Activepieces, flows are built from "integrations", its name for app integrations, roughly 60% of them community-contributed, so the company doesn't directly maintain most of its integration ecosystem.


Your first flow uses the webhook trigger, the[Google Sheets piece](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-sheets) to append the lead as a row, and the[Slack piece](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) to notify the sales channel.


Below, the canvas shows that shape: a Catch Webhook trigger, a middle step, and the Slack step selected. In the lead flow the middle step is Google Sheets, where the capture shows a Read Connection action.


In the selected Slack step's panel you'll find fields for Connection, User, Message and Username, and its connection field points back at step 2.


That's the habit worth teaching a first team: map each field from the step before it, then press Test Step under Generate Sample Data before publishing.


Starting the pilot is cheap for the reasons this article keeps returning to. You're not reading a source-available licence to work out what your use allows, because the core is open source under an MIT licence.


On cloud, the plan is free and needs no card, so the first team can test without a purchase order.


If hosting is the sticking point, you can self-host instead, and the flow you built on cloud is the same kind of flow you'd run on your own server.


### When staying on n8n is the better choice


Stay on n8n if your team already runs production workflows there and they're stable. Rebuilding every flow by hand has a real cost, and a working setup with predictable volume doesn't need a second tool.


If you depend on an n8n node that has no matching integration, the same applies. Check the integration list for each app before you commit.


If volume, licence terms or hosting are what worry you, build this one flow and compare.[Sign up for Activepieces cloud](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fn8n-workflows-how-they-work-and-examples-2026-guide) and run it for a week; at 1 credit per run, the free plan's 1,000 monthly credits cover 1,000 leads.
